# E5-LS1-T6 grounded source cards

## M01 — Dermatologist-level classification of skin cancer with deep neural networks
- Source: Nature (2017)
- URL: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature21056
- Type: peer_reviewed_study
- Evidence strength: high
- Notes: Clinical image classification study directly about diagnostic performance for skin cancer.

## M02 — Development and Validation of a Deep Learning Algorithm for Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy in Retinal Fundus Photographs
- Source: JAMA (2016)
- URL: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2588763
- Type: peer_reviewed_study
- Evidence strength: high
- Notes: Large validation study for AI-based diabetic retinopathy detection with clinical datasets.

## M03 — Artificial Intelligence With Deep Learning Technology Looks Into Diabetic Retinopathy Screening
- Source: JAMA (2016)
- URL: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2588762
- Type: editorial
- Evidence strength: medium
- Notes: Diagnosis-focused editorial discussing why AI screening for diabetic retinopathy matters clinically.

## M04 — AI-enabled medical devices
- Source: U.S. FDA (2025)
- URL: https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/software-medical-device-samd/artificial-intelligence-enabled-medical-devices
- Type: regulatory_reference
- Evidence strength: medium
- Notes: Regulatory overview tracking FDA-authorized AI-enabled medical devices, many in diagnostic workflows.

## M05 — Science and Medicine chapter highlights from the 2025 AI Index Report
- Source: Stanford HAI (2025)
- URL: https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report
- Type: research_report
- Evidence strength: medium
- Notes: Broad but current summary of AI use in science and medicine, including FDA-authorized AI-enabled devices.

## M06 — Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health
- Source: WHO (2021)
- URL: https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240029200
- Type: policy_report
- Evidence strength: medium
- Notes: Healthcare-wide AI governance guidance; relevant to clinical AI but not tightly focused on diagnosis.

## M07 — The state of AI in early 2024
- Source: McKinsey (2024)
- URL: https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai-2024
- Type: industry_survey
- Evidence strength: medium
- Notes: Cross-industry survey about AI adoption and value creation; relevant to healthcare strategy but not diagnostic practice.

## M08 — Translating Artificial Intelligence Into Clinical Care
- Source: JAMA (2016)
- URL: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2588762
- Type: editorial
- Evidence strength: medium
- Notes: Broader clinical translation discussion; closer to implementation than to specific diagnosis tasks.

## M09 — Improving Diagnosis in Health Care
- Source: National Academies (2015)
- URL: https://nap.nationalacademies.org/catalog/21794/improving-diagnosis-in-health-care
- Type: consensus_report
- Evidence strength: medium
- Notes: Foundational report on diagnosis quality and diagnostic error, but not about AI methods.

## M10 — Future Promise of and Potential Pitfalls for Automated Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy
- Source: JAMA Ophthalmology (2016)
- URL: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaophthalmology/fullarticle/2478173
- Type: editorial
- Evidence strength: medium
- Notes: Close to diagnosis, but more a commentary on automation trade-offs than a primary validation study.

## M11 — Renewables 2024
- Source: IEA (2024)
- URL: https://www.iea.org/reports/renewables-2024
- Type: energy_report
- Evidence strength: high
- Notes: Authoritative but unrelated to medical diagnosis; included as an irrelevant source.

## M12 — The 2025 AI Index Report
- Source: Stanford HAI (2025)
- URL: https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report
- Type: research_report
- Evidence strength: high
- Notes: Current AI macro trends and investment data, but not a medical diagnosis source.
